concepts.name: Supervised learning pipeline
concepts.summary: The steps from framing the problem and splitting data into train/validation/test, through training and evaluation, to deployment.

concepts.name: Loss function vs evaluation metric
concepts.summary: A loss scores a single prediction and is minimized in training; a metric summarizes performance to judge whether a model is good enough.

concepts.name: Expected risk
concepts.summary: The average loss of a model over the unknown data-generating distribution, which we can never compute directly.

concepts.name: Empirical risk
concepts.summary: The average loss over the training set, used as a practical stand-in for expected risk and minimized to choose a model.

concepts.name: Squared (L2) vs absolute (L1) loss
concepts.summary: Squared loss penalizes large errors quadratically and reacts more strongly to outliers than absolute loss, which penalizes them linearly.

concepts.name: 1D linear regression, predictions and residuals
concepts.summary: Model a scalar target with a line w1*x + w0; the residual is the gap between prediction and target.

concepts.name: Squared-loss cost J(w1, w0)
concepts.summary: Training 1D linear regression means finding the weights that minimize the average squared residual J(w1, w0).

concepts.name: Cost surface in weight space and convexity
concepts.summary: Viewed over the weights, the squared-loss cost is a convex quadratic bowl, so any local minimum is a global minimum.

concepts.name: Gradient descent and the update rule
concepts.summary: Repeatedly move the weights against the gradient of the cost, scaled by a learning rate, until reaching the minimum.

concepts.name: Multivariate linear regression (vectorization, bias trick)
concepts.summary: Stack inputs into a matrix and append a column of ones so all predictions and the cost are written as matrix expressions.

concepts.name: Normal equation (closed-form solution)
concepts.summary: Setting the gradient of the cost to zero gives w* = (X^T X)^-1 X^T t when X^T X is invertible; fast for moderate dimensions.

concepts.name: Nonlinear regression with feature maps
concepts.summary: Transform inputs with features such as polynomials so a model that is linear in its parameters can fit nonlinear relationships.

concepts.name: Underfitting, overfitting and validation error
concepts.summary: As model complexity grows, training error keeps falling while validation error reaches a sweet spot and then rises.

concepts.name: 0-1 loss and logistic (cross-entropy) loss
concepts.summary: 0-1 loss is intuitive but non-differentiable; cross-entropy is smooth, convex in the logit and punishes confident wrong predictions.

concepts.name: Why linear regression is a bad classifier
concepts.summary: Regressing on 0/1 labels gives predictions outside [0, 1] and a squared loss that ignores the Bernoulli structure, motivating logistic regression.
